images.title: Two sharers or four sharers
images.purpose: Show that the same roti shared by more children gives each child a smaller piece: one half is more than one fourth.
images.composition: Two equal round rotis side by side with wide space between them, and one small comparison row centred below.
images.exact_structure: Left: one round roti cut by one straight line into 2 equal halves, one half filled teal #0072B2, the other plain. Right: one round roti of exactly the same size cut by two straight lines into 4 equal quarters, one quarter filled amber #E69F00, the others plain. Below, centred: the teal half piece and the amber quarter piece placed side by side, the half clearly bigger. Exactly 2 rotis, 2 coloured pieces, 1 comparison row.

images.takeaway: More sharers means a smaller share.
images.description: Two same-size rotis: one cut into 2 equal halves with one half shaded teal, one cut into 4 equal quarters with one quarter shaded amber; below, the half and the quarter side by side show 1/2 is more than 1/4.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at one child's share in each roti and say which is bigger, before reading the bottom line.

image_decisions.why: The comparison of a half and a fourth of the same roti is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
